title: Voice AI ROI for Bathroom Remodeling: How to Measure What It’s Worth
summary: Bringing voice AI into your bath remodeling call center? Here’s how to measure ROI: set a baseline, track the right numbers, and see what real remodelers got.
body_markdown:
By[Pam Torrey](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pam-torrey-920175b4/) , Senior Director of Marketing at Leaping AI


When a bathroom remodeling company begins to[explore voice AI](https://leapingai.com/blog/voice-ai-for-bathroom-remodelers) , the question is always the same: how will I know if it’s working? It’s a fair question when you’re bringing in a tool that could cost thousands of dollars a month and will touch a substantial chunk of a company’s leads. A voice agent can handle thousands of calls a day, but that doesn’t matter unless it can book appointments on the calendar that convert into jobs sold. Measuring voice AI ROI for a bathroom remodeler comes down to three things: knowing where you started, tracking the right metrics, and giving each metric adequate time to move.


## **Start with a baseline before you go live**


You can’t measure a change if you never measured the metrics in the first place. Before implementing a voice AI agent, pull the last 60 to 90 days of your current numbers, broken out by lead source:


-


Time to contact a new lead (speed to lead)


-


Number of contact attempts a lead gets before the team stops following up


-


Contact rate: the percentage of dialed leads that pick up the phone


-


Set rate: the percentage of contacted homeowners who book an in-home appointment


-


Sit rate: the share of those appointments that actually happen


-


Close rate and average ticket


-


Lead cost, broken down by source


-


Number of after-hours or weekend calls that went to voicemail


On top of those standard call center metrics, add in one more number that isn’t usually tracked: how many leads in your CRM were never reached at all. That’s your pile of aged leads, and for many bath remodelers, it’s the biggest opportunity for voice AI to make a difference in the business.


## **Match the metric to the job you brought voice AI in to do**


Voice AI is a versatile tool in a bath remodeling call center. As such, the metrics that prove it’s working will depend on which roles it fills.


### **Speed to lead**


Some of the easiest numbers to track when implementing voice AI are time to first contact and set rate on fresh leads. Lifetime Bath & Glass, a Southeast bath remodeler that buys leads from several vendors, now reaches new leads within 10 seconds. They booked 3 appointments on day one, average 4 to 10 appointments a day, and book up to 50% more on peak days, which is exactly when a human call center falls behind.


### **Aged lead reactivation**


Some of the biggest upside from voice AI comes from working the leads that would have otherwise sat cold in the CRM. Bath Experts, a $60 million Midwest bath remodeler, runs about 4,000 outbound calls a day across real-time and aged leads, reaches roughly 15% of the leads it dials, and books 5 in-home consultations a day, each worth $5,000 to $30,000 or more.


> *“Leaping AI helps us to systematically contact our real-time and aged leads lists and is booking us on average five incremental appointments a day.”*
>
>
> Jay Shah, Head of Marketing, Bath Experts


### **After-hours coverage**


Track the number of calls answered by voice AI on evenings and weekends, and the appointments booked from those calls. The baseline here is the number of[after-hours calls that went to voicemail](https://leapingai.com/blog/why-one-day-bath-companies-are-losing-jobs-to-a-missed-phone-call) .


### **Call center capacity**


Pay attention to the number of appointments your CSRs are booking per hour, and where their time goes once the voice agent takes over the routine calls. At Lifetime Bath, the top-performing CSR was promoted to customer success manager because the voice agent took over the repetitive outbound work, freeing her up to do more high-value tasks.


Tracking the wrong metrics can hide real results.[Independent Home](https://leapingai.com/customers/independent-home-aged-lead-reactivation) , a nationwide bath replacement remodeler with an in-house call center on Long Island, was already fast on new leads with their old dialer. Their speed to lead didn’t change. The gain showed up in the second, third, and fourth attempts their old system never made. If they’d only watched speed to lead, they would have missed it.


> *“Our old dialer couldn’t call old leads. They’d just be out there to die. Now we’re reviving them and turning them into appointments and sales.”*
>
>
> Yale Lipschik, CEO, Independent Home

## **The numbers to track, in three layers**


Think about the data in three layers. Each one answers a different question, and you need all three to know whether voice AI is paying off for your business.


**Layer**


**What to track**


**The question it answers**


Activity


Calls made, attempts per lead, time to first contact, contact rate, share of after-hours calls answered


Is it really working my leads?


Conversation quality


How often homeowners ask for a live person, handoffs to a CSR, Do Not Call requests, call recordings and transcripts


Are homeowners comfortable talking to the agent?


Outcomes


Appointments set, sit rate, close rate, revenue from AI-booked appointments, cost per appointment


Is it generating revenue?


Because they move first, it’s easiest to get excited about activity numbers, but don’t stop there. Call volume is just a topline metric and doesn’t tell you ROI. The outcomes are what pay for it.


Conversation quality is the one owners and marketing leaders worry about most, especially with an older customer base who might be suspicious of[speaking with an AI agent](https://leapingai.com/blog/voice-ai-vs-chatbot-vs-sms-ai-for-contractors) . But it’s also the easiest one to check: listen to a random sample of calls. At Independent Home, most homeowners don’t realize they’re talking to AI, and there has been no meaningful bounce rate from homeowners wanting a live rep.


The comparison that matters most is on outcomes. Put AI-booked appointments next to CSR-booked appointments and compare both sit and close rates. If the AI-booked appointments sit and sell like the CSR-booked ones, you know the voice agent is booking real, qualified opportunities and not just filling time slots.


## **Set up tracking before day one**


Most of the time, if a business is having trouble tracking ROI from their voice agent, it’s because they either don’t know what metrics to track or they didn’t have a tracking mechanism in place before onboarding and launch. A few things to have ready before launch:


-


Tag AI-booked appointments[in your CRM](https://leapingai.com/blog/voice-ai-crm-integration) as their own setter or source, so you can follow them all the way to a sale.


-


Keep lead sources separate, because aged leads, fresh leads, and after-hours calls will perform differently. Blending them hides what’s working.


-


Agree on the scorecard with your[AI voice vendor](https://leapingai.com/blog/how-to-choose-a-voice-ai-partner-for-your-bath-remodeling-call-center) up front: which numbers, reviewed how often, and by whom. Bath Experts holds weekly optimization meetings with the Leaping AI team.


## **When to expect each number to move**


Different numbers move on different timelines, and judging all of them in week one sets you up to call it too early.


**Timeframe**


**What you should be able to see**


First days


Activity. Calls going out, homeowners picking up, first appointments booked. Lifetime Bath booked 3 on day one.


First 30 days


Quality and reliability. Independent Home had reliable connectivity and strong customer satisfaction within 30 days. Bath Experts went from kickoff to live calls in 30 days.


60 to 90 days


Outcomes. In-home consultations take time to run and close, so sold revenue lags behind appointments. Independent Home chose to start paying by day 60, before their free trial ran out.


Ongoing


Tuning. Scripts, call timing, and lead lists get sharper as you review results together.


## **Run the ROI math on your own numbers**


It’s important for each bath remodeler to have the formula to determine ROI for their own call center. Because each business is different, an average across a whole industry won’t give you a good baseline to measure against. Here is the formula to use:


**Revenue from voice AI** = leads worked × contact rate × set rate × sit rate × close rate × average ticket


**ROI** = (revenue from AI-booked sales − cost of voice AI) ÷ cost of voice AI


There are two things to keep in mind when you run the numbers. First, most of the leads the voice agent works are ones you’ve already paid for. The cost of the lead is spent either way, so revenue coming out of them is new money and not an expense. Second, be sure to factor in the time your team gets back. Hours the CSRs used to spend on routine calls can be repurposed to higher-value work that actually grows the bottom line.


For a sense of scale, take Bath Experts’ own numbers. Five in-home consultations a day at $5,000 to $30,000 each is $25,000 to $150,000 in potential project value landing on their calendar every day, before sit rate and close rate apply. Your number will be different, but it comes from leads already sitting in your CRM.


## **Where to go from here**


The companies getting the most out of voice AI knew their baseline, picked the right metric for the job, and gave it time to show up in sold jobs.
